title: A 12-year-old inherited a small chiefdom. He built an empire from Kabul to Tibet. November 13, 2026.
excerpt: On the 246th anniversary of his birth, the story of Maharaja Ranjit Singh - a 12-year-old chieftain who united rival factions into the Sikh Empire, one of the last major powers to resist British expansion in the subcontinent.
bodyHtml:
A 12-year-old inherited a small chiefdom. By the time he was done, he ruled an empire that stretched from Kabul to Tibet

Maharaja Ranjit Singh was born on November 13, 1780. He became the leader of a small Sikh chiefdom in Punjab at age 12, after his father's death, and over the following decades united rival Sikh factions into the Sikh Empire - one of the last major powers to resist British expansion in the subcontinent. At its height, his empire stretched from the Khyber Pass to Tibet, built on a modernized, disciplined army and a famously tolerant administration that included Hindu, Muslim, and Sikh officials alike.

Ranjit Singh didn't inherit an empire - he built one from a fractured region, and ran it as one of the most stable, pluralistic powers of its era, holding off colonial encroachment for his entire 40-year reign.

sources.text: Sikh Museum UK - Maharaja Ranjit Singh's 235th Birth Anniversary
